newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zaire suspends aid for refugees in east, U.N. says.
newsitem.headline: Zaire suspends aid for refugees in east, U.N. says.

text.p: Western aid agencies in east Zaire were ordered by local officials on Friday to suspend aid work for 160,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, camped near fighting between rebels and Zairean troops, the U.N. refugee agency said.
UNHCR would meet officials in the Lubutu area, 240 km (150 miles) southeast of east Zaire's regional hub of Kisangani, to try to clarify the situation, agency spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said.
"The situation is precarious. The refugees are in desperate need. If there are any kind of restrictions, it could cause tremendous problems," she told a Geneva briefing.

Local officials told UNHCR that "the illegal installation of U.N. agencies in the area, illegal introduction of journalists into refugee sites, illegal use of airstrips and illegal opening of agency offices" were the reasons behind the suspension.
They informed the UNHCR that U.N. planes were also barred from landing on airstrips in the region, O'Toole added.
She said delivering aid to the refugees was increasingly risky because of worsening security and fighting in the region.

UNHCR had no details of the fighting, but reports from the region on Thursday said Tutsi-led rebels, fighting a Zairean counter-offensive, were advancing towards Lubutu -- a key town on the road to Kisangani, the Zairean army's main base.
Some 120,000 Hutus are camped out in Tingi-Tingi, a tiny Zairean village some seven km (four miles) east of Lubutu, and another 40,000 in Amisi, 70 km (44 miles) to the southeast.
O'Toole said the World Food Programme would no longer transport or stockpile food to the Amisi region because of insecurity.
To make things worse, Uganda had told the WFP it could no longer fly relief supplies into eastern Zaire from its territory, O'Toole said.
Zaire accuses Uganda and Rwanda of sending troops into its territory to aid the rebels. Both countries deny the charges.
"Vehicles and even planes are being requisitioned by the military," O'Toole said.

"The situation in eastern Zaire is becoming increasingly serious. We'll have serious problems within a week if we're unable to increase the quantity of food being brought into the camps. Malnutrition could become a big problem."
The Rwandan refugees in Lubutu trekked deeper west into Zaire after Tutsi rebels overran their camps in October rather than join 600,000 who returned home to Rwanda.

The UNHCR says they are accompanied by soldiers of Rwanda's former Hutu government army which played a key role in 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis, after which the Hutus fled to eastern Zaire in fear of retribution.
